creator: Alexander Terp
description:
`muster tab new --pane <ref>` fails when the keyboard is on a different machine from the pane named, and blames the pane for it:

    muster: the daemon devenv holds no pane called p2005jfz1e, so there is no
    workspace to put a tab in and nothing was made. Most likely it closed while
    this was in flight.

The pane had not closed. It was a local pane, alive and on screen, named while the window's keyboard sat on a devenv pane.

This contradicts the CLI's own contract, which `muster --help` states in its first paragraph: *"A REF is a pane's name, as `muster window` prints it... It is Muster's own name for the pane and is unique across every machine the window is showing, so it needs nothing else beside it."* Every other verb honours that. With the keyboard on the devenv and a local pane named:

    muster pane new    --pane <local>   ->  made a pane on local
    muster pane read   --pane <local>   ->  printed the local pane
    muster pane rename --pane <local>   ->  renamed it
    muster tab new     --pane <local>   ->  refused, naming the wrong daemon

`CreateTab` in `crates/muster-seam/src/handler.rs` takes the two halves from different places. The pane comes from the ref (`named.or_else(session::focused_pane)`), and the daemon comes from `resolve_daemon(&create.daemon_id)`, which falls back to `session::focused_daemon()` when the request names none - which it does, because `cmd+T` and the CLI both leave `daemon_id` empty. `workspace_of(&daemon, &pane)` is then asked for a pane on a machine that does not hold it, and reports it as missing. The pane's own daemon is never consulted, though the mirror knows it.

The error message makes it worse than a refusal. "Most likely it closed while this was in flight" sends you to look at the pane, which is fine, rather than at the keyboard, which is what decided the answer.

Fix: when a request names a pane, take the daemon from that pane. Fall back to the focused daemon only when no pane is named, which is what `cmd+T` needs and is the case `resolve_daemon` was written for.

## Reproducing it

1. Attach two machines with a pane on each - `muster window` lists both.
2. Put the keyboard on machine B's pane: `muster tab focus <B's tab>`, or click it.
3. Name machine A's pane: `muster tab new --pane <A's pane>`.
4. It refuses, naming B as the daemon that does not hold A's pane.
5. Same ref, other verbs, same keyboard position: `muster pane new --pane <A's pane>` and `muster pane read --pane <A's pane>` both work.

## Validating a fix

- With the keyboard on B, `muster tab new --pane <A's pane>` makes a tab on A, and `muster window` shows it under A.
- With no `--pane`, `tab new` still lands on the machine the keyboard is on - that behaviour is `cmd+T`'s and must not change.
- The other verbs keep working unchanged; a regression here would be silent, since they take the same kind of ref.
- Worth a check per verb that accepts a REF, asserting each acts on the named pane's machine rather than the focused one - the conformance corpus already carries the CLI's contract text about refs being unique across machines.
title: 🎯 tab new takes the machine from the keyboard, not from the pane you named
